messages.subject: menu bar woes - JS not loading properly?
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to build a basic application containing a menu bar and a label, wherein the label will change when a button in the menu bar is clicked.

I'm shamefully script-kiddy'ing JS and HTML code written by Vincent Nijs (found here https://github.com/mostly-harmless/radyant/tree/master/inst/marketing, and thus refer all credit for it's awesomeness to him).

In my implementation, input$tool does not update when a menu button is clicked, and remains NULL after any/all menu button(s) are clicked. Also, the menus do not disappear when clicked when running the application, and if I intentionally misspell the navbar.js filename (eg. rewrite it as navbar123.js in global.r) this does not throw an error (which seems inconsistent because includeHTML will throw an error if I misspell navbar.html).

I do not think this is a browser issue (using latest version of google chrome), because the menu implementation found here http://vnijs.rady.ucsd.edu:3838/marketing/ behaves as expected.

This leads me to suspect that the navbar.js file is not being loaded properly and/or that I am committing a gravely embarrassing rookie-level mistake.

Also, I feel like inputId in getTool (global.r) should be passed as an additional argument into includeHTML or tags$script; at the moment it seems to me that the inputId argument doesn't serve any purpose and Shiny is associating "input$tool" based on id="tool" (in line 2 in navbar.html).

I'm generally very hesitant with posting problems on mailing lists, but I've been at this all day, and any help would be appreciated :)

Cheers, Jeff



----- global.r

getTool <- function(inputId) {
  tagList(
    singleton(tags$head(tags$script(src = "js/navbar.js"))),
    tags$html(includeHTML('www/navbar.html'))
  )
}


----- server.r

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
observe({print(paste("tool", input$tool))})
getText<-reactive({
currText<-"none"
if (!is.null(input$tool)) {
currText <- input$tool
}
return(currText)
})
output$char <- renderText({getText()})
})

------ ui.r

shinyUI(
    pageWithSidebar(
        headerPanel('TEST!'),
        sidebarPanel(
getTool("tool")
),
        mainPanel(
textOutput("char")
)
    )
)

------ navbar.js

var navbarBinding = new Shiny.InputBinding();

$.extend(navbarBinding, {

  find: function(scope) {
    return $(scope).find(".navbar");
  },
  getValue: function(el) {
    return $(el).data("nav-value");
  },
  setValue: function(el, value) {
    $(el).text(value);
  },
  subscribe: function(el, callback) {
    $(el).on("click.navbarBinding", "a[data-value]", function(e) {
      $(el).data("nav-value", $(e.target).data("value"));
      $('.dropdown.open').removeClass('open');
      callback();
    });

  },
  unsubscribe: function(el) {
    $(el).off(".navbarBinding");
  }
});
 
Shiny.inputBindings.register(navbarBinding, "navbarBinding");

On Saturday, December 7, 2013 11:59:56 PM UTC-8, Jeff wrote:
Hi,

I'm trying to build a basic application containing a menu bar and a label, wherein the label will change when a button in the menu bar is clicked.

I'm shamefully script-kiddy'ing JS and HTML code written by Vincent Nijs (found here https://github.com/mostly-harmless/radyant/tree/master/inst/marketing, and thus refer all credit for it's awesomeness to him).

In my implementation, input$tool does not update when a menu button is clicked, and remains NULL after any/all menu button(s) are clicked. Also, the menus do not disappear when clicked when running the application, and if I intentionally misspell the navbar.js filename (eg. rewrite it as navbar123.js in global.r) this does not throw an error (which seems inconsistent because includeHTML will throw an error if I misspell navbar.html).

I do not think this is a browser issue (using latest version of google chrome), because the menu implementation found here http://vnijs.rady.ucsd.edu:3838/marketing/ behaves as expected.

This leads me to suspect that the navbar.js file is not being loaded properly and/or that I am committing a gravely embarrassing rookie-level mistake.

Also, I feel like inputId in getTool (global.r) should be passed as an additional argument into includeHTML or tags$script; at the moment it seems to me that the inputId argument doesn't serve any purpose and Shiny is associating "input$tool" based on id="tool" (in line 2 in navbar.html).

I'm generally very hesitant with posting problems on mailing lists, but I've been at this all day, and any help would be appreciated :)

Cheers, Jeff



----- global.r

getTool <- function(inputId) {
  tagList(
    singleton(tags$head(tags$script(src = "js/navbar.js"))),
    tags$html(includeHTML('www/navbar.html'))
  )
}


----- server.r

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
observe({print(paste("tool", input$tool))})
getText<-reactive({
currText<-"none"
if (!is.null(input$tool)) {
currText <- input$tool
}
return(currText)
})
output$char <- renderText({getText()})
})

------ ui.r

shinyUI(
    pageWithSidebar(
        headerPanel('TEST!'),
        sidebarPanel(
getTool("tool")
),
        mainPanel(
textOutput("char")
)
    )
)

------ navbar.js

var navbarBinding = new Shiny.InputBinding();

$.extend(navbarBinding, {

  find: function(scope) {
    return $(scope).find(".navbar");
  },
  getValue: function(el) {
    return $(el).data("nav-value");
  },
  setValue: function(el, value) {
    $(el).text(value);
  },
  subscribe: function(el, callback) {
    $(el).on("click.navbarBinding", "a[data-value]", function(e) {
      $(el).data("nav-value", $(e.target).data("value"));
      $('.dropdown.open').removeClass('open');
      callback();
    });

  },
  unsubscribe: function(el) {
    $(el).off(".navbarBinding");
  }
});
 
Shiny.inputBindings.register(navbarBinding, "navbarBinding");
